pr_title: drivers: uart: stm32: fix handling interrupt and async api in isr
pr_body:
When using the uart driver with interrupt and async api
at the same time (instance for interrupt and instance for async),
the transmission complete interrupt was handled in the async
handling section, even when interrupt driven api is used.
This caused transmission to not work properly in interrupt mode.
The fix is to move the interrupt mode handling to the begginning
of the isr. If async mode is used then interrupt mode code
will not be run.

Signed-off-by: Shlomi Vaknin <shlomi.39sd@gmail.com>

Fixes: #35321

issue_context.title: Improve STM32: Serial Driver,Handle uart mode per instance
issue_context.body:
The goal is to have each serial (instance)  mode to be configured independently as either, interrupt, or async.

 the issue I noticed is, the shell uses interrupt API, while when we enable the`CONFIG_UART_ASYNC_API=y` there is no mean to make a particular UART instance driven using interrupt mechanism, as such the shell is completely not functional.

**Additional context**
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/34672 
The issue above describes the problem related to the shell with the current arrangement of serial driver

I can contribute a PR to address this, I would like to hear some inputs.
comments: @manoj153 I fixed the issue. The bug is described in the commit message. In general the only place that has shared code between interrupt api and async api is the isr function. So when there is a strange issue between the two modes the isr is the place to look

review_comments:
Having both CONFIG_UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN and CONFIG_UART_ASYNC_API on at the same time will result in the IT_TC of an interrupt driven channel being turned off at some point of time unexpectedly, by line 820 `LL_USART_DisableIT_TC(UartInstance);`.
The zephyr documentation doesn't say CONFIG_UART_INTERRUPT_DRIVEN and CONFIG_UART_ASYNC_API are mutually exclusive. Also, the original intention of this update was to make both INT and DMA channels work at the same time, without introducing per chancel based configuration for INT/DMA.
This potential issue causes my code in a lock up situation: a completion semaphore is never released because the TC is turned off before the data in the TX buffer is completely sent.
